prompt: /deep-research Consider the countries that received a rating of “very high” in the 2023 Global Peace Index. Exclude any countries that have an area of either over 1,000,000 km2 or under 25,000 km2. Of the remaining countries, which had the highest CO2 emissions per capita in 2023 according to data.worldbank.org?
instruction: Consider the countries that received a rating of “very high” in the 2023 Global Peace Index. Exclude any countries that have an area of either over 1,000,000 km2 or under 25,000 km2. Of the remaining countries, which had the highest CO2 emissions per capita in 2023 according to data.worldbank.org?
answer:
Now I have all the data needed. Let me compile the findings and provide the answer.

## Summary of Research

### 1. Countries with "Very High" 2023 Global Peace Index Rating
From the Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP) 2023 GPI report, **17 countries** received a "very high" rating (GPI score ≤ 1.5): Iceland, Denmark, Ireland, New Zealand, Austria, Singapore, Portugal, Slovenia, Japan, Switzerland, Canada, Czechia, Finland, Croatia, Germany, Netherlands, Bhutan [1].

### 2. Land Area Filter (25,000–1,000,000 km²)
Using World Bank land area data (AG.LND.TOTL.K2) [2], the countries that fall outside the range:
- **Excluded (>1,000,000 km²)**: Canada (8,788,700 km²)
- **Excluded (<25,000 km²)**: Singapore (718 km²), Slovenia (20,134.5 km²)

**14 countries remain**: Iceland, Denmark, Ireland, New Zealand, Austria, Portugal, Japan, Switzerland, Czechia, Finland, Croatia, Germany, Netherlands, Bhutan

### 3. 2023 CO₂ Emissions per Capita
The World Bank's EN.ATM.CO2E.PC indicator only has data through 2020 [3]. The most current 2023 data comes from the Global Carbon Budget via Our World in Data [4]. Values for the 14 filtered countries:

| Country | 2023 CO₂ per capita (t) |
|---------|------------------------|
| **Iceland** | **9.05** |
| Japan | 7.94 |
| Czechia | 7.70 |
| Germany | 7.02 |
| Netherlands | 6.47 |
| Ireland | 6.46 |
| Austria | 6.23 |
| New Zealand | 6.10 |
| Finland | 5.68 |
| Denmark | 4.85 |
| Croatia | 4.74 |
| Portugal | 3.61 |
| Switzerland | 3.60 |
| Bhutan | 2.07 |

---

## Answer

**Iceland** had the highest CO₂ emissions per capita in 2023 (9.05 metric tons) among countries that:
- Received a "very high" rating in the 2023 Global Peace Index, **and**
- Have a land area between 25,000 km² and 1,000,000 km².

---

## Sources

[1] Institute for Economics & Peace. *Global Peace Index 2023* (PDF), pp. 8–13. https://www.economicsandpeace.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/GPI-2023-Web.pdf

[2] World Bank. *Land area (sq. km)* — indicator AG.LND.TOTL.K2 (2023). https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/AG.LND.TOTL.K2

[3] World Bank. *CO₂ emissions (metric tons per capita)* — indicator EN.ATM.CO2E.PC. Latest available year: 2020. https://databank.worldbank.org/metadataglossary/world-development-indicators/series/EN.ATM.CO2E.PC

[4] Our World in Data / Global Carbon Budget (2025). *CO₂ emissions per capita* — 2023 values. https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/co-emissions-per-capita
